# fptcloud_backup_native_volume_restore (Resource)

Restores a Backup Native volume restore point into a new volume. The API has no in-place restore for volumes. Applying the resource runs the restore once and waits for it to finish; destroying it only removes it from state. Change a value in `triggers` to run the restore again. The API does not return the new volume's id; find it by `name` with the `fptcloud_storages` data source. Run one restore per volume at a time; two concurrent restores of the same volume can be matched to the wrong history row. Once the restore has been sent, the resource is saved whatever the outcome, and the next apply does not restore again. A failed restore, a timeout or an interrupted apply (Ctrl+C) ends the apply with a warning, not an error, and stores the outcome in `status` and `message`. The restore goes on without Terraform after a timeout or an interrupt; each later plan or apply reads the restore history and stores the outcome once the restore ends. A restore that timed out before its history row appeared is matched to the first restore of the same source after it was sent. Only interrupt an apply once: a second Ctrl+C stops Terraform before it saves the restore, and the next apply restores again.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "fptcloud_backup_native_volume_restore_points" "data" {
  vpc_id    = var.vpc_id
  volume_id = var.pv_volume_id
}

# Any triggers value works and a new value restores again. A request time, as
# below, is recommended so the state records when each restore was requested.
resource "fptcloud_backup_native_volume_restore" "data_copy" {
  vpc_id           = var.vpc_id
  volume_id        = var.pv_volume_id
  restore_point_id = data.fptcloud_backup_native_volume_restore_points.data.restore_points[0].id
  name             = "pv-data-restored"
  size_gb          = 20
  triggers         = { restore = "2026-10-26 09:00:00" }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the new volume, at most 50 characters: letters, digits and hyphens.
- `restore_point_id` (String) ID of the restore point, from `fptcloud_backup_native_volume_restore_points`.
- `size_gb` (Number) Size of the new volume in GB. The API requires at least the size of the source volume.
- `volume_id` (String) ID of the volume the restore point belongs to.
- `vpc_id` (String) ID of the VPC.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `triggers` (Map of String) Values that run the restore again when they change, which no other argument can express because every other argument stays equal. Any string works; only a change matters. We recommend the time you ask for the action, in the form `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, for example `2026-10-26 09:00:00`, so the state records when each one was requested. Avoid `timestamp()`: it changes on every plan and repeats the action on every apply.

### Read-Only

- `finished_at` (String) End of the restore, RFC 3339 UTC.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `message` (String) Why the action did not succeed, or why the provider stopped waiting for it. Empty after a success.
- `started_at` (String) Start of the restore, RFC 3339 UTC.
- `status` (String) Result of the restore: the status of its history row once it ended, `success` or `failed`. The provider stores its own value when the API has none to give: `tf_timeout` when the provider stopped waiting before the action ended, `tf_interrupted` when the apply was interrupted while it waited, `tf_failed` when the action failed without an API status. A plan or apply checks `tf_timeout` and `tf_interrupted` again and replaces them with the API's status once the action ends.
